newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees $35 bln in telecom privatization revs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees $35 bln in telecom privatization revs.

text.p: Brazil expects to garner an estimated $35 billion in revenue from the privatization of its telecommunications sector, a Communication Ministry spokesman said.
The spokesman, confirming comments late Thursday by Communications Minister Sergio Motta, said the figure "does not refer to the value of the telecoms but to the amount the government will receive."
He added that the total market value of Brazil's telecoms system, including the 10 cellular B Band concessions, is estimated at $120 million.
In all, the federal government expects to take in some $70 billion from its entire privatization program, Motta was quoted as saying.
The government plans to open bids later this month and award contracts in June and July for concessions to operate cellular services on the B Band.
It also expects to split up the giant Telebras system of state-level and long-distance subsidiaries and sell it off by the end of 1998.
The first units to be spun off are expected to be its largest local operator, Telesp, and long-distance monopoly Embratel, which are likely to go on the auction block in 1998's first quarter.
